hook: You used to be sharp. Now you feel like a slower version of yourself.
topic: Brain fog as input degradation, not cognitive decline
body:
**If you used to be sharp — quick, retentive, clear — and now you feel like a slower version of that person, I want you to hear this precisely: that sharpness is not gone. You have just been running your brain on progressively worse inputs.**

Age-related cognitive decline is a real and gradual process. But what most people under fifty experience as "my brain is getting worse" is not that. It is a deterioration in the quality of the conditions the brain depends on to perform.

Sleep architecture degrades. Dietary patterns shift. Movement decreases. Chronic low-grade stress elevates cortisol, which directly suppresses the prefrontal cortex — the part of your brain responsible for exactly the thinking you feel you've lost.

None of those are fixed. All of them are responsive to specific changes.

The person who thinks quickly and doesn't lose words mid-sentence — that is still your default state. Brain fog is not who you are becoming. It is what happens when the inputs get bad enough, for long enough.

Fix the inputs. Link in bio.
